title: Word Break
oneLinerQuestion: Determine if a string can be segmented into a space-separated sequence of dictionary words.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Word Break problem requires determining whether a string s can be segmented into a space-separated sequence of one or more dictionary words. Because multiple prefixes can match different dictionary entries, exploring possibilities greedily can lead to dead ends. Instead, this problem possesses optimal substructure: suffix s[i..n] can be segmented if there exists a valid word matching s[i..i+len] and the remaining suffix s[i+len..n] is also segmentable. By framing this with 1D Dynamic Programming and working backward from the end of the string, each subproblem is solved once and reused to determine the validity of preceding indices in polynomial time.

- Step 1: Base Case & DP Table Initialization — Let n = s.length. We initialize a boolean array `dp` of size `n + 1`, where all values default to `false`. We set the base case `dp[n] = true`, representing that an empty suffix after the end of the string is trivially valid.

- Step 2: Backward Iteration Structure — We iterate index `i` backwards from `n - 1` down to `0`. At each position `i`, `dp[i]` evaluates whether the suffix starting at `i` (`s[i..n]`) can be successfully formed using words from `wordDict`.

- Step 3: Word Dictionary Matching — For each position `i`, we iterate through every `word` in `wordDict`. Let `len = word.length`.

- Step 4: Boundary & Substring Verification — We check if the word can fit starting at `i`: `if (i + len <= n && s.substring(i, i + len) === word)`. If the prefix matches the dictionary word, we inherit the segmentation validity of the subsequent remaining suffix: `dp[i] = dp[i + len]`.

- Step 5: Early Loop Break — If `dp[i]` evaluates to `true`, we have confirmed that a valid segmentation exists starting at index `i`. We immediately break out of the inner loop over words to avoid redundant checks for that index.

- Step 6: Termination & Return — Once the outer loop completes, `dp[0]` indicates whether the full string `s[0..n]` can be segmented into valid words, and we return `dp[0]`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N * M * K) where N is the length of string s, M is the number of words in wordDict, and K is the average length of a word (due to substring comparisons). Space Complexity: O(N) auxiliary space to store the boolean DP table of size N + 1.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION wordBreak(s, wordDict):
    dp = ARRAY_OF_SIZE(LENGTH(s) + 1, INITIAL_VALUE = False)
    dp[LENGTH(s)] = True
    FOR i FROM LENGTH(s) - 1 DOWN TO 0 DO:
        FOR w IN wordDict DO:
            IF (i + LENGTH(w)) <= LENGTH(s) AND SUBSTRING(s, i, i + LENGTH(w)) == w THEN:
                dp[i] = dp[i + LENGTH(w)]
            IF dp[i] THEN BREAK
        END FOR
    END FOR
    RETURN dp[0]
END FUNCTION
